newsitem.title: USA: Mexico to open 4 more natgas distribution tenders.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to open 4 more natgas distribution tenders.

text.p: The Mexican government hopes to open up three more tenders for private sector distribution of natural gas as a precursor to opening the Mexico City market around next August, a Mexican energy ministry official said.
On Thursday, the government determined the geographic zone for the Hermosilla region. Next up would be the industrial region of Ciudad Madero/Altamira before year-end, and Toluca next year.

"New investment will be needed to cover rapidly growing demand for natgas, which is expected to increase from 2.4 billion cubic feed per day (bcfd) in the year 2005, said Alfredo Phillips Greene, head of the investment promotion office of the Secretariat of Energy.
Demand is estimated to reach 4.2 bcfd in 10 years, Phillips said, while addressing delegates at a Latin American investment conference in New York.
The Ciudad Madero/Altamira region in northeast Mexico is expected to require $50 million in investments.
"Current consumption is 277 million cfd but you could see a big jump because of potential new investment in petrochemicals," he said.
The Mexican government is in the process of selling minority stakes in 61 petrochemical plants, but recent policy flip-flops have caused some foreign investors to re-think their level of interest.
The government has already awarded one gas concession for the Mexicali area, and bidding is underway for a second concession in Chihuahua.
The concessions are part of a government program to liberalize gas transport distribution and storage and reduce dependence on fuel oil and diesel.
The government is seeking to increase the participation of gas in six sources, such as power plants, to 50 percent by the year 2005, from 37 percent currently.
